title: spec review: Remove the Codex gates: fallback mode only with an enabled codex row, requeue not hold without one, free_slots caps Claude rows by max_parallel_claude_workers, executed_by from the row provider
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label B2. With Codex cancelled the pool is Claude-only (codex rows disabled
in the live pool.toml). Today the daemon and executor still treat 'no Codex' as an outage.

Facts (main 355583c):
- orchestrator/daemon.py:459-464 _codex_available(pool) is true when ANY enabled execute row (Claude rows
  included) is not cooling; daemon.py:467-471 _fallback_mode(pool) = not _codex_available and
  cfg.codex.on_exhausted == 'fallback_claude'. With only Claude rows, all cooling, it reports fallback mode.
- daemon.py:488-503 free_slots(): outside fallback mode returns sum(max_parallel - running) over every enabled
  execute row that is not cooling (Claude rows included, uncapped: 3 + 2 = 5 > max_parallel_claude_workers 4,
  pool.toml [limits]); only fallback mode applies the cap via running_claude_workers (474-478) and
  inflight_claude_dispatches (481-485).
- daemon.py:697-707 eligible() and 906-908/929-930 dispatch() use fallback/fallback_tier: unchanged contract,
  they only follow _fallback_mode.
- daemon.py:1943-1945 notifies 'Executor (Codex) cooling; execute tasks held' whenever not
  pool.codex_available() and pool.codex.cooling(), regardless of whether any codex row is enabled.
- daemon.py:397 (reconcile_dead orphan re-gate) posts executed_by = t.get('executor') or 'claude:<tier>', so a
  codex task gets a bare 'astra' while executor.py:324 and :678 and daemon.py:576/:647 post 'codex:<id>'.
- orchestrator/executor.py:487-496 start(): a Claude row -> _exhausted(pool, t, tier=...); ex None ->
  _exhausted(pool, t). executor.py:545-597 _exhausted(): when not routed it reads pool.cfg['codex']['on_exhausted']
  (551, KeyError without [codex]) and HOLDS the task 'codex unavailable; policy=...; no Claude fallback for
  complexity N' (553-555) when no fallback tier applies. The requeue shape already exists at 559-566
  (status queued, pipeline.hold_note 'claude_capacity', dispatched_at popped).

Change:
1. daemon.py: add a helper returning the enabled execute-role rows with provider 'codex'. _fallback_mode(pool) is
   True only when that list is non-empty, every row in it is cooling, and on_exhausted == 'fallback_claude' (read
   with .get and default 'hold'). _codex_available keeps its name but counts only codex rows.
2. free_slots(pool): fallback mode unchanged. Otherwise codex_slots = free parallelism of non-cooling enabled codex
   rows; claude_slots = min(free parallelism of non-cooling enabled Claude execute rows,
   max(0, max_parallel_claude_workers - running_claude_workers(pool) - inflight_claude_dispatches())); return
   codex_slots + claude_slots. Keep the [limits] default of 4 when the table is missing.
3. daemon.py:1943: the Codex cooling notice fires only when at least one codex row is enabled.
4. executed_by from the row provider: add executor.executed_by(task, cfg) -> str: executor field naming a codex row
   -> 'codex:<id>'; a 'claude:<tier>' executor -> itself; no executor -> 'claude:<tier>' (use
   pool.executor_identity(field, cfg) for the provider). Use it at daemon.py:397 and keep 'codex:<id>' output at
   executor.py:324/678 and daemon.py:576/647 (route those through the helper too if trivial).
5. executor._exhausted(): read the policy with pool.cfg.get('codex', {}).get('on_exhausted', 'hold'). When not
   routed (tier None on entry) and no enabled codex row exists, requeue exactly like 559-566 (status queued,
   hold_note 'claude_capacity', pop dispatched_at, no hold_reason) and return {'status': 'claude_capacity',
   'reason': 'no eligible executor'}; never hold in that case. With an enabled codex row the legacy path (policy
   fallback tier or the 'codex unavailable' hold) is unchanged.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE; update to the new contract):
- tests/test_executor.py claude_pool() (~388-400) builds cfg['executors'] = [claude:opus] only, so these tests rely
  on the legacy fallback with NO codex row and change meaning under rule 5:
  test_complexity_nine_fallback_still_held (expects the 'codex unavailable ... complexity 9' hold),
  test_claude_dispatch_below_cap_dispatches (expects fallback tier sonnet),
  test_claude_dispatch_requeues_at_worker_cap (expects reason 'claude workers at cap'). Give claude_pool an
  option to add one enabled, cooling codex row and use it in these three so they keep testing the legacy path;
  the new acceptance test covers the Claude-only path.
- tests/test_daemon.py free_slots/fallback tests (~2109-2195: test_free_slots_uses_claude_capacity_under_fallback,
  test_free_slots_zero_under_hold_policy, test_free_slots_subtracts_running_claude_executes,
  test_daemon_once_dispatches_under_fallback_when_codex_cooling, test_saturated_codex_returns_zero_not_fallback,
  test_fallback_counts_running_claude_roles_and_inflight_dispatches, test_fallback_skips_complexity_without_tier,
  test_free_slots_survives_missing_cfg_tables) run on the harness pool.toml, which keeps codex rows and strips
  Claude rows (tests/_harness.py), so they should pass unchanged; if one fails, update it to the new contract,
  never weaken the cap.
- tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_worker_posts_codex_done (~3770) pins executed_by 'codex:astra': must stay.

Out of scope: pool.py (B1), spawn.py (B4), mcp.py/tool_catalog.py (B3), concurrency.py/speculation.py.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_claude_only_pool_never_enters_fallback_and_caps_free_slots: passes: with every codex row disabled and enabled claude:sonnet (max_parallel 3) and claude:opus (max_parallel 2) rows, _fallback_mode(pool) is False, free_slots(pool) == min(5, max_parallel_claude_workers - running Claude workers - in-flight dispatches) (4 with the shipped cap and nothing running, 1 with three running), and a daemon tick with every Codex row disabled sends no 'Codex cooling' notice

tests/test_executor.py::test_no_codex_row_requeues_instead_of_holding: passes: executor.start on a pool whose executors are only Claude rows, with pick_executor returning None, leaves the task queued with pipeline.hold_note 'claude_capacity', no dispatched_at and no hold_reason, returns status 'claude_capacity', and does not raise when pool.cfg has no [codex] table

risks.issue: Rule 5 requeues every unrouted no-executor case as claude_capacity with no bound and no signal. A complexity outside every row's band, all rows disabled or all rows cooling would re-dispatch every tick and never surface. It used to be held visibly.
claude_slots subtracts inflight_claude_dispatches(), which also counts Codex-bound dispatches. In a mixed pool, Claude capacity is under-reported while codex_slots is added separately.
The mixed pool (non-cooling codex plus Claude rows) sums both slot counts, but pick_executor assigns tasks to rows later. No acceptance test covers this case.

executor.executed_by does not say what to return for an unknown or stale executor field, such as the bare 'astra' already on tasks, or for a codex task with no executor field. The spec also does not confirm a pool or cfg is in scope at daemon.py:397.
The 'no Codex cooling notice' check passes against the old code unless the test cools the legacy pool.codex while every codex row is disabled.

The harness strips Claude rows, so the acceptance test has to build the fixture by hand. The 'three running' case needs bus tasks with executor 'claude:sonnet' or 'claude:opus', because the row's running count is derived from the executor id.
No rollback path or decisions.md entry. If a live pool.toml loses its codex rows by mistake, fallback silently turns off.

suggested_spec_changes: In _exhausted, requeue as claude_capacity only when an enabled Claude execute row exists and the miss is transient (cooling, saturated or no account headroom). If there is no enabled executor at all, or the complexity is outside every row's band, keep the visible hold with a hold_reason such as 'no eligible executor'. Alternatively, add a requeue counter or notification.

Count only Claude-bound dispatches in the claude_slots cap. Alternatively, state that inflight_claude_dispatches deliberately over-subtracts in mixed pools, and add a mixed-pool free_slots test (non-cooling codex row plus Claude rows) that asserts the sum.

Define executed_by for the remaining cases. An unknown non-empty executor field is returned unchanged. A codex task with no executor field is out of scope. Name the pool or cfg source available in reconcile_dead.
Require the notice test to set pool.codex cooling while every codex row is disabled, and to assert notify is not called with the 'Executor (Codex) cooling' message.

Describe the Claude-row fixture for the free_slots acceptance test: executors built in cfg, running tasks on the bus with executor 'claude:<tier>', and an in-flight dispatch with dispatched_at and no gated_at.
Add a rollback note: revert via git revert <sha> and add a dated decisions.md entry, since fallback semantics change.
